findings.reason: Untrusted source: in tpacket_snd() with PACKET_VNET_HDR set, vnet_hdr points into the mmap'd TX ring frame (packet_current_frame -> po->tx_ring.pg_vec user-shared pages), concurrently writable by unprivileged userspace with no lock/READ_ONCE between fetches. Violated single-fetch invariant: the first fetch validates via __packet_snd_vnet_parse(vnet_hdr, tp_len) at line 2826, which enforces virtio_net_hdr.h checks at af_packet.c:2532-2541 (hdr_len <= tp_len; csum_start+csum_offset+2 <= hdr_len); the second independent fetch at lines 2830-2831 re-reads vnet_hdr->hdr_len from the same shared frame into copylen with no re-validation. Unsafe use: copylen is consumed as an skb sizing/copy parameter - sock_alloc_send_skb(..., hlen + tlen + sizeof(struct sockaddr_ll) + (copylen - dev->hard_header_len)) at lines 2834-2837 and, in tpacket_fill_skb (lines 2600-2613), hdrlen = min_t(int, copylen, tp_len), skb_put(skb, copylen - dev->hard_header_len) and skb_store_bits(skb, 0, data, hdrlen). A racing userspace write between the validation read (line 2826) and the re-read (line 2830) can make copylen exceed the validated tp_len (up to 65535): only tp_len bytes are copied from the frame into the linear area while copylen - dev->hard_header_len bytes are skb_put, so the remainder of the transmitted linear area is uninitialized heap memory (kernel heap disclosure on the wire), and copylen also sizes the allocation/put arithmetic. Additionally a third re-read of all vnet_hdr fields from the same shared memory occurs at line 2869 (virtio_net_hdr_to_skb(skb, vnet_hdr, ...)) after skb fill, so the transmitted skb mixes fields from different fetches. Counterevidence checked: tpacket_parse_header (2649-2715) single-fetches tp_len and tp_mac/tp_net into locals and validates before returning (safe); the non-ring packet_snd path snapshots the header via copy_from_iter_full (2555) (safe); __packet_get_status uses READ_ONCE (440-446); virtio_net_hdr_to_skb itself re-validates csum_start/csum_offset against the skb via pskb_may_pull and skb_partial_csum_set (include/linux/virtio_net.h:96-112), which is why the copylen/hdr_len use at 2830-2831 is the unvalidated consumption.

candidates.reason: tpacket_snd(): vnet_hdr->hdr_len fetched for validation at line 2826 (__packet_snd_vnet_parse -> hdr_len <= tp_len check at line 2540) and independently re-fetched at lines 2830-2831 into copylen, used unvalidated in sock_alloc_send_skb sizing (2834-2837) and tpacket_fill_skb skb_put/skb_store_bits (2600-2613).

Third fetch of the same shared-memory vnet_hdr (csum_start/csum_offset/gso_size/flags) after skb fill; folded into the main finding - the csum values are re-validated internally (pskb_may_pull/skb_partial_csum_set), but the cross-fetch inconsistency with the copylen-sized skb remains.

tpacket_parse_header reads tp_len (2663/2666/2669) and off = tp_mac/tp_net (2685-2705) each exactly once into locals, validates them (2672-2675, 2707-2708) and returns the locals; the caller consumes the returned locals (2814, 2845), no second dereference of ring header fields.

packet_snd_vnet_parse() snapshots the virtio_net_hdr from the user iterator via copy_from_iter_full (2555) into kernel stack memory; validation (2558) and later use both operate on the snapshot, not racy shared memory.
tpacket_rcv() is the kernel-writer side of the ring: tp_mac/tp_net/macoff are computed from kernel skb/po state, not read from user-writable memory in a check-then-use pattern.

The csum_start/csum_offset re-read at virtio_net.h:97-105 is re-validated at the point of use: pskb_may_pull(skb, start + max(thlen, off+2)) at line 101 and skb_partial_csum_set(skb, start, off) at line 104 bound the values against the actual skb, so raced values cannot bypass bounds here in isolation.

limitations: Bounded to the tpacket_snd/af_packet TX send path and its helpers in snapshots/s01; packet_set_ring/packet_mmap ring-setup paths, net/packet/diag.c, and TPACKET_V3 block-retire (__packet_lookup_frame_in_block/prb_*) were not exhaustively audited for the same invariant.

No dynamic reproducer was built; the uninitialized-linear-area disclosure consequence (copylen raced above validated tp_len) and the exact skb-sizing arithmetic are from static reading only, hence medium confidence.
Impact of the third fetch at line 2869 beyond internal re-validation (mixed-fetch skb state) is not fully characterized.
